api/TAssetBundle.Extensions.PrefixAliasR.summary: Class PrefixAliasResolver Namespace TAssetBundle.Extensions Assembly TAssetBundle.Extensions.dll Prefix-based alias resolver that maps user-facing path prefixes to one or more canonical folders, with an optional search-path fallback. public sealed class PrefixAliasResolver : IAssetPathResolver Inheritance object PrefixAliasResolver Implements IAssetPathResolver Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Two operating modes per prefix: Single folder: pure string substitution. Works without a catalog. Multiple folders: search path. Uses AssetExists to find the first folder that contains the asset. Falls back to the first folder when no match is found or when AssetExists is not set. Single-folder and unmatched results are cached. Multi-folder results are checked against AssetExists on every call, so catalogs added later are honored. A prefix that ends with '/' keeps that '/' between the folder and the rest of the path (Add("@char/", "Assets/Characters") resolves "@char/hero.prefab" to "Assets/Characters/hero.prefab"). Any other prefix is replaced by the folder as is. Longer prefixes match first, allowing nested namespaces to coexist. Properties AssetExists Catalog existence predicate injected by the caller. Required only when any prefix has more than one folder. Typically wired to ExistAsset(string). public Func<string, bool> AssetExists { get; set; } Property Value Func<string, bool> Count Number of registered prefixes. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Methods Add(string, IEnumerable<string>) Registers a prefix that maps to an ordered list of folders. Matches Google Play Plugins for Unity convention so PlayCore's AssetPackManager.getAssetLocation(pack, "assetpack/{file}") resolves correctly. public const string AssetPackFolderName = "assetpack" Field Value string Methods GenerateAssetPackName(string) Generates an asset pack name from an asset bundle name using the leaf folder plus an 8-char xxHash32 of the full parent path. e.g. "bundles/characters/hero" -> "characters_a1b2c3d4" Length stays bounded (leaf + 9 chars) so deeply nested bundle paths don't blow up Windows MAX_PATH during gradle build, and the hash disambiguates leaf-name collisions across different parent paths (e.g. "ui/icons" vs "menu/icons"). Leaf is sanitized independently (Google Play rules: must start with letter, only [a-zA-Z0-9_]) before the hash is appended, so the hash is never partially stripped even when the leaf is all-digits, leading-underscore, or non-ASCII (e.g. Korean folder names) — uniqueness is preserved by the hash regardless. public static string GenerateAssetPackName(string assetBundleName) Parameters assetBundleName string Returns string GenerateAssetPackNameFromParentPath(string) Asset pack name from a bundle's parent path (the directory containing one or more asset bundles). UnloadAll() Unloads all assets and asset bundles to free memory. Asset requests that have already started loading when this is called complete once as failures, and requests made afterwards start new loads instead of joining them (a new load of the same asset bundle waits until the canceled one has ended). A scene request in progress completes once with an error logged and releases its scene bundle; if Unity was already loading the scene itself, Unity may still activate that scene (unload it yourself if unwanted). changelog.html.title: Changelog | TAssetBundle 5.2 (stable)
changelog.html.summary: Changelog All notable changes to TAssetBundle are documented in this file. 5.2.0 Asset collection: added editable extension exclusions and reversible file/folder Ignore. .lighting defaults apply once to legacy settings; custom and empty lists remain unchanged. Remote delivery and cache: added optional hash filenames and selective cache-clearing APIs; improved concurrent downloads, cached loading and WebGL cache deletion. Loading and unloading: added TAssetBundles.OnUnloadedAll and fixed failed-request cleanup. [Pro] improved prefab ownership and AssetManager/pool cleanup. Builds and samples: fixed build paths, cached catalogs and sample sprite references; player builds now wait for built-in preparation and stop on failure. Compatibility: fixed Unity 6000.0/6000.1 compilation. [Pro] fixed path aliases/DLC overrides; async prefab APIs require Unity 2022.3.20+ or Unity 6+. 5.1.0 🆕 Added Catalog Diff Viewer (TAssetBundle > Catalog Diff) — compare two catalogs before shipping an update. Search and filter Added / Removed / Modified / Unchanged bundles, inspect exact hash and size changes, identify missing assets or manifests with basic copy/reveal context actions, and expand visible results with Expand Details. Available in both Lite and Pro. 5.0.2 Fixed UpdateTempCatalogAsync accepting a remote catalog whose build number is older than the active local — GetDownloadSize* was computing against an outdated remote. 5.0.1 [Play Asset Delivery] Fixed install-time asset packs failing to load on live installs and hash-changed install-time bundles being skipped from the predownload step. [Play Asset Delivery] Plugin inspector's Manifest Summary now shows the resolved asset pack name (auto/custom) per manifest. Custom names are validated inline against Google Play rules in the manifest Inspector, and the PAD settings area is now a collapsible header. [Editor] Skip pre-build cache preparation when useBuildCache is disabled — faster build entry on large projects. 5.0.0 ⚠️ Breaking (minimum Unity): Raised to Unity 2021.3 LTS (from 2019.4). ⚠️ Breaking (folder structure): Extensions moved to Assets/TAssetBundleExtensions/. Delete the legacy Assets/TAssetBundle/Scripts/Extensions/ after upgrade; the using TAssetBundle.Extensions; namespace is unchanged. Editor-time detector warns if the legacy folder remains. 🆕 Lite edition introduced — Lite (free) ships the core engine + plugins; Pro adds the productivity layer (AssetManager, LinkAsset, PrefabPoolManager, PathAliasTable, Asset Usage Tracker). See in-package lite_vs_pro.md. 4.7.0 [AssetManager] Added Path Aliases — prefix-to-folder mapping with multi-folder priority search for DLC overrides. Configure via PathAliasTable or PrefixAliasResolver. Failed asset loads auto-clean from cache; retries no longer need UnloadUnusedAssets Loading the same path as different types now errors cleanly instead of throwing InvalidCastException Hardened prefab pool against races during multi-coroutine init and pool replacement 4.6.1 [Play Asset Delivery] Pack bundles (install-time, fast-follow, on-demand) are now recompressed from LZMA to LZ4 before packing — every pack type lands on the device before loading, so LZ4's faster decompression wins over LZMA's smaller size for runtime performance. Manifest Inspector plugins now support multi-edit — selecting multiple manifests in the Project window applies plugin settings (e.g., PAD delivery type) to all of them in one action. Breaking for plugin authors: IManifestEditorPluginModule.OnManifestInspectorGUI now receives a TAssetBundleManifest[] instead of a single manifest. 4.6.0 [Android] Added Google Play Asset Delivery plugin — install-time / fast-follow / on-demand delivery with automatic AAB integration, OnDownloadProgress event, concurrent download dedup, and Split Application Binary compatibility Added UpdateTempCatalogAsync — check for catalog updates and calculate download sizes without replacing the active catalog Fixed TagUtil.SetDirty to check IsPersistent before marking dirty Added [Serializable] to CompositionStrategy Data class and removed unnecessary SetDirty calls 4.5.0 Added Cross-Reference Analyzer — detect and visualize cross-bundle asset references at build time Redesigned Dependency Checker with TreeView + SearchField Browser manifest headers now show Builtin/Encrypt/Tags at a glance Added ManifestPluginData system — per-manifest plugin data with build hook Improved plugin Inspector UI Converted async void to async Task for safer exception handling Added enum-based errorType to UnityWebRequestError Improved catalog/AssetBundle data corruption resilience and IO error protection Added AssetBundleRuntimeInfo.TryGetCustomData() Renamed "Shrink All" to "Collapse All" 4.4.0 Added asset search API to TAssetBundleManifest (SearchAssets, TryGetAssetInfo) Added asset search feature to TAssetBundle Browser 4.3.1 Fixed GetNotIncludedAssets() to correctly evaluate asset inclusion across the entire manifest tree, including child manifests. Resolved cases where parent folders or already-included assets could be incorrectly reported as not included. Improved internal asset inclusion checks and related logic. 4.3.0 Added a new sample demonstrating FilePathCollector usage for runtime path-based asset loading. Improved sample code with additional comments for better clarity and understanding. Enhanced download result handling to include detailed error information. Build process optimizations and minor internal refactoring for improved stability. 4.2.0 Added FilePathCollector, which collects asset path information at runtime. Added an extensible plugin system. Fixed an issue where the RemoteUrl in the catalog was cached, making previously downloaded assets inaccessible before the new RemoteUrl was applied. Other optimizations and minor bug fixes. 4.1.1 Fixed DefaultAssetCatalogComparer comparison operation bug. 4.1.0 Optimized the build process to significantly reduce build times. 4.0.0 Changed TAssetBundle.AssetManager to TAssetBundle.TAssetBundles for a clearer API. Added an extended AssetManager with easy asset loading, unloading, prefab pooling, and object usage tracking using TAssetBundle. Added Asset Usage Tracker to the editor, allowing users to view, sort, and search objects currently using specific assets during play mode with regex. Added a new PrefabPoolManager for efficient pooling of frequently used prefabs.. Made asset bundles containing video assets uncompressed. Added sorting and regex search features to the Asset Reference Tracker. Various bug fixes, refactoring, and optimization. 3.11.1 Fixed null reference error in list field when generating TAssetBundleManifest in Unity versions after 2022. 3.11.0 When building AssetBundles, an option has been added to output built-in AssetBundles to a separate folder. The option is named "Builtin Asset Bundles Use Separate Folder" Built-in AssetBundles that are compressed with LZMA (smaller size) now undergo recompression to LZ4 the first time they are accessed for use. Fixed to not use Unity's default AssetBundle provider since native caching is not available on the WebGL platform. Instead, a specific managed AssetBundle provider is used. This fixes a bug in previous versions where the download size was unknown when using Unity's default AssetBundle provider. 3.10.0 Added an option to automatically abort web requests when download latency exceeds a specified time. (This feature is intended to resolve situations where there is no response for up to 2 minutes when switching to Wi-Fi.) Fixed an issue where apps would throw an exception saying there was no catalog when not using TAssetBundle. 3.9.2 Fixed a bug where references would be lost when using AssetRef inside an asset that has already been AssetBundled when playing in AssetBundle mode in the editor. 3.9.1 Fixed so that if an exception occurs during AssetBundle building, the exception is also passed to the parent. (this is mainly an issue where the next command is executed even if an exception occurs when building with a script) Improved way of catching duplicate assets in TAssetBundleManifest. 3.9.0 Added Asset Dependency Finder (Right click on the asset in the project window [TAssetBundle] Run Dependency Finder) 3.8.1 Fixed bug where assets were not excluded from the build cache if only their properties were changed 3.8.0 Build number has been added to settings. When loading a catalog, it has been modified to use the catalog with the higher build number between the local catalog and the remote catalog. 3.7.3 Fixed bug where local AssetBundle could not be found on Android 3.7.2 Fixed initialization in AssetManager to support Unity EnterPlayMode. 3.7.1 Fixed bug where disk space check was incorrect in SpecificAssetBundleProvider 3.7.0 The scene path to be saved in the catalog has been modified to be saved as is rather than converted to lowercase letters. Changed the remote url to one for more efficient networking and simplicity. Cleaned up source code and added help menu 3.6.1 Fixed a bug where an error occurred during build if an embedded asset bundle exists when using 'Append Hash From File Name' in the build options in Settings. Fixed a bug where an error occurred in the log when reading a remotely updated AssetBundle as if it were an AssetBundle included in the build. 3.6.0 WebGL platform supports all Unity versions and bug fixes Limitations related to the WebGL platform: When using UnityRemoteAssetBundleProvider in versions after 2022, the cache information of remotely received asset bundles cannot be obtained. We recommend disabling the Use UnityRemoteAssetBundleProvider option. 3.5.0 Added tag rename function to tag editor Added context menu to tag editor Added a function to check the manifest using the tag in the tag editor 3.4.0 Added ignore assets to allow specific assets to be ignored in the manifest Efficient modifications to the method for finding embeddable assets 3.3.0 Fixed a bug where the AssetBundle could not be released when the AssetBundle scene loaded with Additive was unloaded Fixed a bug where dependent AssetBundles would not be rebuilt if they were not cached Support scene loading from scene path Support for loading progress of assets and scenes Added scene activation callback after scene loading 3.2.1 Fixed bug with AssetRef not updating in editor 3.2.0 Added Manual Added Api Documentation Added api comment Added TAssetBundle, TAssetBundle.Editor asmdef Class scope refactoring 3.1.0 Added Runtime Asset Reference Tracker Added AssetBundle Dependency Checker 3.0.0 Added TAssetBundle Browser Added AssetReference Added Web Server Test Newly developed simple tag system Added downloads as Assets and AssetReference Optimize asset bundle loading Build cache bug fixed TAssetBundleManifest bug fixed WebGL support 2.0.0 added catalog compress and encryption added asset bundle encryption added inherit based tag system check download size based on tags, download based on tags optimize and refactoring minor bug fixes

changelog_ko.html.title: Changelog | TAssetBundle 5.2 (stable)
changelog_ko.html.summary: Changelog TAssetBundle의 모든 주요 변경 사항을 이 파일에 기록합니다. 5.2.0 에셋 수집: 제외 확장자 편집과 되돌릴 수 있는 파일·폴더 Ignore를 추가했습니다. 구설정에는 .lighting을 1회 자동 적용하며 사용자 지정·빈 목록은 유지합니다. 원격 배포·캐시: 해시 파일명 옵션과 선택적 캐시 삭제 API를 추가하고 동시 다운로드·캐시 로드·WebGL 캐시 삭제를 개선했습니다. 로드·해제: TAssetBundles.OnUnloadedAll을 추가하고 실패 요청의 리소스 정리를 수정했습니다. [Pro] 프리팹 소유권과 AssetManager·풀 정리를 개선했습니다. 빌드·샘플: 빌드 경로·캐시 카탈로그·샘플 스프라이트 참조를 수정했습니다. 플레이어 빌드는 내장 번들 준비를 기다리고 실패 시 중단합니다. 호환성: Unity 6000.0·6000.1 컴파일 문제를 수정했습니다. [Pro] 경로 앨리어스·DLC 오버라이드를 수정했으며, 비동기 프리팹 API는 Unity 2022.3.20 이상 또는 Unity 6 이상에서 제공합니다. 5.1.0 🆕 Catalog Diff Viewer 추가 (TAssetBundle > Catalog Diff) — 업데이트 배포 전에 두 카탈로그를 비교합니다. Added / Removed / Modified / Unchanged 번들을 검색·필터링하고, 정확한 해시와 크기 변화를 확인하며, 누락된 에셋이나 매니페스트는 기본 복사/위치 확인 컨텍스트 메뉴로 식별하고, Expand Details로 화면의 결과를 펼칠 수 있습니다. Lite와 Pro 모두에서 사용할 수 있습니다. 5.0.2 UpdateTempCatalogAsync가 로컬 카탈로그보다 buildNumber가 낮은 원격 카탈로그도 임시 카탈로그로 채택해, GetDownloadSize*가 오래된 원격 기준으로 계산되던 문제 수정. 5.0.1 [Play Asset Delivery] install-time 에셋팩이 라이브 환경에서 로드되지 않거나 catalog 업데이트로 hash가 바뀐 번들이 사전 다운로드에서 누락되던 문제 수정. [Play Asset Delivery] Plugin 인스펙터의 Manifest Summary에서 매니페스트별로 해석된 에셋팩 이름을 표시 (auto/custom). Custom 이름은 매니페스트 인스펙터에서 Google Play 규칙으로 인라인 검증되고, PAD 설정 영역은 접을 수 있는 헤더로 정리. [Editor] 빌드 캐시를 끈 경우(useBuildCache=false) 사전 캐시 준비 단계를 건너뜀 — 대형 프로젝트의 빌드 진입 시간 단축. 5.0.0 ⚠️ Breaking (최소 Unity 버전): Unity 2021.3 LTS로 상향 (기존 2019.4). ⚠️ Breaking (폴더 구조): Extensions가 Assets/TAssetBundleExtensions/로 이동했습니다. 업그레이드 후 기존 Assets/TAssetBundle/Scripts/Extensions/ 폴더를 삭제하세요. using TAssetBundle.Extensions; 네임스페이스는 그대로 유지됩니다. 에디터 감지기가 기존 폴더가 남아 있으면 경고를 표시합니다. 🆕 Lite 에디션 추가 — Lite(무료)는 코어 엔진과 플러그인을 제공하고, Pro는 productivity 레이어(AssetManager, LinkAsset, PrefabPoolManager, PathAliasTable, Asset Usage Tracker)를 추가합니다. 패키지 내 lite_vs_pro_ko.md 참조. 4.7.0 [AssetManager] Path Aliases 추가 — 접두어를 폴더에 매핑하며, 다중 폴더 우선순위 검색으로 DLC 오버라이드를 지원합니다. PathAliasTable 또는 PrefixAliasResolver로 설정합니다. 실패한 에셋 로드는 캐시에서 자동 정리되어, 재시도 시 더 이상 UnloadUnusedAssets를 호출할 필요가 없습니다 동일 경로를 다른 타입으로 로드하면 InvalidCastException 대신 명확한 에러를 반환합니다 다중 코루틴 초기화와 풀 교체 중 발생하던 prefab pool race를 강화했습니다 4.6.1 [Play Asset Delivery] Pack 번들(install-time, fast-follow, on-demand)은 패킹 전 LZMA에서 LZ4로 재압축됩니다 — 모든 pack 타입은 로딩 전에 디바이스에 안착하므로, LZMA의 작은 크기보다 LZ4의 빠른 압축 해제 속도가 런타임 성능에 유리합니다. Manifest Inspector 플러그인이 다중 편집을 지원합니다 — Project 창에서 여러 manifest를 선택하면 플러그인 설정(예: PAD 전송 타입)을 한 번에 모두 적용합니다. 플러그인 작성자에게 breaking: IManifestEditorPluginModule.OnManifestInspectorGUI가 단일 manifest 대신 TAssetBundleManifest[]를 받습니다. 4.6.0 [Android] Google Play Asset Delivery 플러그인 추가 — install-time / fast-follow / on-demand 전송 방식, 자동 AAB 통합, OnDownloadProgress 이벤트, 동시 다운로드 중복 제거, Split Application Binary 호환성 지원 UpdateTempCatalogAsync 추가 — 활성 카탈로그를 교체하지 않고 카탈로그 업데이트 여부와 다운로드 크기를 확인합니다 TagUtil.SetDirty가 dirty 표시 전 IsPersistent를 확인하도록 수정 CompositionStrategy Data 클래스에 [Serializable] 추가, 불필요한 SetDirty 호출 제거 4.5.0 Cross-Reference Analyzer 추가 — 빌드 시점에 번들 간 에셋 참조를 감지하고 시각화 Dependency Checker를 TreeView + SearchField 기반으로 재설계 Browser의 manifest 헤더에서 Builtin/Encrypt/Tags를 한눈에 표시 ManifestPluginData 시스템 추가 — manifest별 플러그인 데이터 + 빌드 훅 플러그인 Inspector UI 개선 안전한 예외 처리를 위해 async void를 async Task로 전환 UnityWebRequestError에 enum 기반 errorType 추가 카탈로그/AssetBundle 데이터 손상 복원력 및 IO 에러 보호 강화 AssetBundleRuntimeInfo.TryGetCustomData() 추가 "Shrink All"을 "Collapse All"로 명칭 변경 4.4.0 TAssetBundleManifest에 에셋 검색 API 추가 (SearchAssets, TryGetAssetInfo) TAssetBundle Browser에 에셋 검색 기능 추가 4.3.1 GetNotIncludedAssets()이 자식 manifest를 포함한 manifest 트리 전체에 걸쳐 에셋 포함 여부를 정확히 평가하도록 수정 부모 폴더나 이미 포함된 에셋이 미포함으로 잘못 보고되던 케이스를 해결 내부 에셋 포함 검사 및 관련 로직 개선 4.3.0 런타임 경로 기반 에셋 로딩을 위한 FilePathCollector 사용 예제 샘플 추가 더 명확한 이해를 돕기 위해 샘플 코드에 추가 주석 보강 다운로드 결과 처리에 상세 에러 정보 포함하도록 개선 빌드 프로세스 최적화 및 안정성 향상을 위한 사소한 내부 리팩터링 4.2.0 런타임에 에셋 경로 정보를 수집하는 FilePathCollector 추가 확장 가능한 플러그인 시스템 추가 카탈로그의 RemoteUrl이 캐싱되어, 새 RemoteUrl 적용 전까지 이전에 다운로드된 에셋에 접근할 수 없던 문제 수정 그 외 최적화 및 사소한 버그 수정 4.1.1 DefaultAssetCatalogComparer 비교 연산 버그 수정 4.1.0 빌드 시간을 크게 단축하는 빌드 프로세스 최적화 4.0.0 API를 명확히 하기 위해 TAssetBundle.AssetManager를 TAssetBundle.TAssetBundles로 변경 TAssetBundle 기반으로 손쉬운 에셋 로드/언로드, prefab pooling, 객체 사용 추적을 제공하는 확장 AssetManager 추가 에디터에 Asset Usage Tracker 추가 — 플레이 모드에서 특정 에셋을 사용 중인 객체를 정규식으로 보고/정렬/검색 가능 자주 사용하는 prefab의 효율적인 풀링을 위한 새로운 PrefabPoolManager 추가 비디오 에셋이 포함된 에셋 번들을 비압축으로 처리 Asset Reference Tracker에 정렬 및 정규식 검색 기능 추가 다양한 버그 수정, 리팩터링 및 최적화 3.11.1 Unity 2022 이후 버전에서 TAssetBundleManifest 생성 시 list 필드의 null reference 에러 수정 3.11.0 에셋 번들 빌드 시 builtin 에셋 번들을 별도 폴더로 출력하는 옵션 추가. 옵션 이름은 "Builtin Asset Bundles Use Separate Folder" LZMA로 압축된(작은 크기) builtin 에셋 번들이 처음 사용 시 LZ4로 재압축되도록 변경 WebGL 플랫폼에서는 native 캐싱이 동작하지 않으므로 Unity의 기본 AssetBundle provider를 사용하지 않도록 수정. 대신 전용 managed AssetBundle provider를 사용. Unity의 기본 AssetBundle provider 사용 시 다운로드 크기를 알 수 없던 이전 버전의 버그를 수정합니다. 3.10.0 다운로드 지연 시간이 지정된 시간을 초과하면 web request를 자동 중단하는 옵션 추가. (Wi-Fi 전환 시 최대 2분 동안 응답이 없는 상황을 해결하기 위한 기능입니다.) TAssetBundle을 사용하지 않는 경우 카탈로그가 없다는 예외가 발생하던 문제 수정 3.9.2 에디터에서 AssetBundle 모드로 플레이할 때, 이미 AssetBundle화된 에셋 내부에서 AssetRef 사용 시 참조가 사라지던 버그 수정 3.9.1 AssetBundle 빌드 중 예외가 발생하면 부모에게도 예외가 전달되도록 수정. (스크립트로 빌드할 때 예외가 발생해도 다음 명령이 실행되던 문제 해결) TAssetBundleManifest에서 중복 에셋을 잡아내는 방식 개선 3.9.0 Asset Dependency Finder 추가 (Project 창에서 에셋을 우클릭 → [TAssetBundle] Run Dependency Finder) 3.8.1 에셋의 속성만 변경된 경우 빌드 캐시에서 제외되지 않던 버그 수정 3.8.0 설정에 빌드 번호 추가. 카탈로그 로드 시 로컬 카탈로그와 원격 카탈로그 중 빌드 번호가 더 높은 쪽을 사용하도록 변경 3.7.3 Android에서 로컬 AssetBundle을 찾지 못하던 버그 수정 3.7.2 Unity EnterPlayMode를 지원하도록 AssetManager의 초기화 수정 3.7.1 SpecificAssetBundleProvider의 disk space 검사가 잘못 동작하던 버그 수정 3.7.0 카탈로그에 저장될 씬 경로를 소문자로 변환하지 않고 원본 그대로 저장하도록 수정 더 효율적이고 단순한 networking을 위해 remote url 형식 변경 소스 코드 정리 및 도움말 메뉴 추가 3.6.1 Settings의 빌드 옵션에서 'Append Hash From File Name' 사용 시 embedded asset bundle이 존재하면 빌드 중 에러가 발생하던 버그 수정 원격에서 업데이트된 AssetBundle을 빌드에 포함된 AssetBundle처럼 읽을 때 로그에 에러가 출력되던 버그 수정 3.6.0 WebGL 플랫폼이 모든 Unity 버전을 지원하도록 변경 및 버그 수정 WebGL 플랫폼 관련 제한 사항: 2022 이후 버전에서 UnityRemoteAssetBundleProvider 사용 시 원격으로 받은 asset bundle의 cache 정보를 얻을 수 없습니다. Use UnityRemoteAssetBundleProvider 옵션을 비활성화할 것을 권장합니다. 3.5.0 태그 에디터에 태그 이름 변경 기능 추가 태그 에디터에 컨텍스트 메뉴 추가 태그 에디터에서 태그를 사용하는 manifest를 확인하는 기능 추가 3.4.0 특정 에셋을 manifest에서 무시할 수 있도록 ignore assets 추가 embeddable 에셋을 찾는 방식의 효율적 개선 3.3.0 Additive로 로드한 AssetBundle 씬을 언로드해도 AssetBundle이 해제되지 않던 버그 수정 캐시되지 않은 의존 AssetBundle이 재빌드되지 않던 버그 수정 씬 경로를 통한 씬 로딩 지원 에셋 및 씬의 로딩 진행률 지원 씬 로딩 후 씬 활성화 콜백 추가 3.2.1 에디터에서 AssetRef가 갱신되지 않던 버그 수정 3.2.0 매뉴얼 추가 API 문서 추가 API 주석 추가 TAssetBundle, TAssetBundle.Editor asmdef 추가 클래스 스코프 리팩터링 3.1.0 Runtime Asset Reference Tracker 추가 AssetBundle Dependency Checker 추가 3.0.0 TAssetBundle Browser 추가 AssetReference 추가 Web Server Test 추가 새로운 단순 태그 시스템 도입 Assets 및 AssetReference 단위 다운로드 추가 에셋 번들 로딩 최적화 빌드 캐시 버그 수정 TAssetBundleManifest 버그 수정 WebGL 지원 2.0.0 카탈로그 압축 및 암호화 추가 에셋 번들 암호화 추가 상속 기반 태그 시스템 추가 태그 단위 다운로드 크기 확인, 태그 단위 다운로드 최적화 및 리팩터링 사소한 버그 수정

index.html.summary: TAssetBundle All-in-One AssetBundle Management System for Unity TAssetBundle covers the entire AssetBundle lifecycle—configuration, build, download, loading, tracking, and unloading—in one consistent workflow. Manual Showcase API Documentation Change Logs Video Tutorials Forum Discord Requirements Unity Version: 2021.3 LTS or later Supported Platforms: Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, WebGL Quick Start // Initialize await TAssetBundles.InitializeAsync().ToTask(); // Load and link to a GameObject — auto-released on destroy AssetManager.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(image.gameObject, "Assets/Sprites/icon.png") .OnCompleted += asset => { image.sprite = asset.Get(); }; Get started with the full guide Key Features AssetManager — Recommended Workflow Load assets with automatic lifecycle management. Link assets to GameObjects for auto-release on destroy. Built-in prefab pooling, usage tracking, and flexible unloading strategies. Manifest-Based Bundle Configuration Create a TAssetBundleManifest in any folder—all files and subfolders become managed targets. Use composition strategies to define how assets are grouped into bundles. Multiple manifests per folder supported. Incremental Build Cache Only changed bundles are rebuilt. Bidirectional dependency tracking ensures correct propagation through the entire dependency graph. Path-Based Asset Loading Reference assets by project path (Assets/...). AssetRef provides Inspector drag & drop with GUID-based serialization that survives asset moves and renames. Flexible Download System Download by tags, specific assets, or scenes. Check download sizes before starting, with built-in progress tracking. Automatic Memory Management (LinkAsset) Link assets to GameObjects. When the GameObject is destroyed, the asset is automatically released. No manual unload logic required. Built-in Prefab Pooling AssetManager loads prefabs from bundles with integrated pooling. PrefabPoolManager provides standalone pooling for any prefab reference. Asset Usage Tracker Monitor GameObject-to-Asset relationships at runtime. Sort and filter with regex to debug memory usage and find unused assets. Plugin System Extend TAssetBundle with plugins that hook into the build pipeline, runtime loading, and Inspector UI. Play Asset Delivery plugin included. Editor Tools Tool Description TAssetBundle Browser Search, filter, and sort assets across all manifests Cross-Reference Analyzer Detect and visualize cross-bundle asset references Asset Usage Tracker Monitor asset usage at runtime Dependency Checker Visualize bundle dependencies Web Server Test Test remote loading locally Asset Reference Tracker Track active assets and bundles Catalog Diff Compare two catalogs — added / removed / modified bundles and their assets Content Update Flow Configure Asset Bundles — Manually or with Composition Strategies Build Asset Bundles — Incremental build with cache Upload to Remote Storage Complete! View all change logs All copyrights for TAssetBundle are owned by tigu77.

manual/manual.html.title: TAssetBundle Manual | TAssetBundle 5.2 (stable)
manual/manual.html.summary: TAssetBundle Manual TAssetBundle is a powerful, integrated asset bundle management system. Editions (v5.0+) TAssetBundle ships in two editions: Lite (free) — Core runtime + Manifest/Strategy + incremental build + all editor tools (Browser, Cross-Reference Analyzer, Dependency Checker, Asset Reference Tracker, Catalog Diff) + Play Asset Delivery plugin + full source. The runtime API is TAssetBundles (low-level handles). Pro — Lite + the TAssetBundle.Extensions module: AssetManager (context-based loading with GameObject auto-release), LinkAsset, PrefabPoolManager, PathAliasTable, and the runtime Asset Usage Tracker. This manual covers both editions. Sections that describe Pro-only features are clearly marked at their headings. If you are using Lite, follow the TAssetBundles examples and skip the AssetManager / PrefabPoolManager / Path Aliases / Asset Usage Tracker sections. Requirements Unity Version: 2021.3 LTS or later Supported Platforms: Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, WebGL Quick Start Get started with TAssetBundle in 3 steps: Step 1: Create TAssetBundleManifest Right-click on a folder containing assets you want to bundle, then select Create > TAssetBundle > TAssetBundleManifest. Step 2: Configure and Build Select the created TAssetBundleManifest Add a composition strategy (e.g., all_together) Right-click and select Run Composition Strategy Go to TAssetBundle > Build Asset Bundle menu Step 3: Load Assets Lite — low-level TAssetBundles API (also works in Pro): using UnityEngine; using TAssetBundle; public class QuickStartLite : MonoBehaviour { public string spritePath; async void Start() { await TAssetBundles.InitializeAsync().ToTask(); // Load by path — returns a handle var handle = await TAssetBundles.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(spritePath).ToTask(); GetComponent<SpriteRenderer>().sprite = handle.Get(); // Unload when no longer needed // TAssetBundles.UnloadAsset(handle); } } Pro — high-level AssetManager (auto-released when this GameObject is destroyed): using UnityEngine; using TAssetBundle; using TAssetBundle.Extensions; public class QuickStartPro : MonoBehaviour { public string spritePath; async void Start() { await TAssetBundles.InitializeAsync().ToTask(); // Load and link to this GameObject — auto-released on destroy AssetManager.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(gameObject, spritePath) .OnCompleted += asset => { GetComponent<SpriteRenderer>().sprite = asset.Get(); }; } } That's it! For development, you can also use Editor Asset mode to skip building. If a catalog file exists but cannot be read (for example it is locked by another process), InitializeAsync still completes. The error and the original exception are logged, and that catalog is treated as missing: a downloaded catalog that cannot be read falls back to the built-in catalog, and with no readable catalog no asset is found. Initialization does not run again after it has completed; call TAssetBundles.LoadCatalogInfoAsync(catalogName) to retry reading the catalog. Table of Contents Core Concept: Manifest How Manifests Work Explicit Asset Collection (Lite and Pro) Multiple Manifests per Folder Per-Manifest Options Creating a Manifest Composition Strategies AssetManager (Recommended) Context-Based Loading Manual Linking Prefab Pooling Unloading Strategies Usage Tracking Path Aliases TAssetBundles (Low-Level API) Using Asset Path Using Asset Reference PrefabPoolManager Remote Download TAssetBundle Settings Building Asset Bundles Plugin System Editor Tools TAssetBundle Browser TAssetBundle Menu Catalog Diff Asset Usage Tracker Editor Play Modes Sample Materials on URP Core Concept: Manifest How Manifests Work TAssetBundleManifest is the central unit of TAssetBundle. When you create a TAssetBundleManifest in a folder, every file and subfolder under that folder becomes a managed target of that manifest. The manifest defines how those assets are grouped into AssetBundles. Runtime code never needs to know about bundle structure. You always load assets by path — which bundle they belong to, how bundles are split, and what the dependencies are is all handled automatically. This means you can freely restructure your bundles at any time without changing a single line of runtime code. There are two ways to configure bundles: Auto Configuration — Use built-in CompositionStrategy assets to automatically configure bundles. Several strategies are included by default (all_together, all_separately, regex_match, clear, etc.). Add strategies to the manifest and run them to auto-generate the bundle configuration. Strategies are executed in order, so you can combine them: for example, bundle everything together first, then exclude specific assets. Manual Configuration — Drag assets directly into the manifest's AssetBundleBuildInfo list to manually define exactly which assets go into which bundle. Explicit Asset Collection (Lite and Pro) Settings > Explicit Asset Collection > Excluded Extensions applies the same explicit-root policy to direct registrations, expanded folder leaves and composition-strategy candidates. New settings default to .lighting; legacy settings receive this default once on first load, without a separate approval step. Customized or intentionally empty lists are preserved on subsequent loads and updates. An intentionally empty list is supported; Restore Default Exclusions (.lighting) restores the default. Matching ignores case and accepts extensions with or without a leading dot. The manifest Ignore Assets list works without a strategy. Ignoring files/folders removes their leaves from final roots without deleting registrations, including managed descendant Ignore entries. The Excluded [N] foldout explains paths and reasons. Compiler inputs and narrowly identified editor authoring objects are not explicit data roots; runtime TextAssets, ScriptableObjects, shaders, lightmap textures, LightingData and NavMesh data are not blanket-excluded. Excluded from explicit collection; may still be included as a dependency. Unity's scene/lighting dependency closure is preserved; this does not force-strip dependencies or change runtime FilePathCollector patterns. Explicit-root fingerprints invalidate incremental caches even if the dependency union is unchanged (older caches rebuild once). Settings/Undo/Redo/project changes refresh derived search/included caches without dirtying unchanged manifests. Multiple Manifests per Folder You can create multiple manifests in the same folder, each with its own bundling strategy. This lets you apply different rules to different subsets of assets within the same directory tree. For example, in an Assets/Characters/ folder: Manifest A — Bundles all textures together (using regex to match .png files) Manifest B — Bundles each prefab separately (using file filter on .prefab) Per-Manifest Options Each manifest also controls: Builtin — Include bundles in StreamingAssets (shipped with the app, no download needed) Encrypt — Encrypt bundle contents for security Tags — Categorize bundles for selective downloads (e.g., "hd", "lang-en", "level1") Creating a Manifest Right-click on a folder > Create > TAssetBundle > TAssetBundleManifest Manifest Inspector: # Option Description 1 Enabled Include in AssetBundle build target 2 Built-in Include AssetBundles in the app 3 Encrypt Encrypt the configured AssetBundles 4 Tags Set tags for download filtering 5 Composition Strategies List of strategies to auto-configure bundles 6 Asset Bundle Build List Configured AssetBundle information Manual Configuration: You can manually add assets by clicking Add Asset Bundle Build Info and dragging assets. Auto Configuration: Use composition strategies for automatic configuration. Add a strategy, then right-click the manifest and select Run Composition Strategy. Composition Strategies Composition strategies automatically configure how assets are grouped into AssetBundles. Strategy Description all_separately Add assets as individual asset bundles all_together Add assets as one asset bundle clear Clear asset bundle build information exclude_objects Exclude specific assets from build info file_separately Add only files as individual asset bundles file_together Add only files as one asset bundle fixed_objects Add only specific assets to one asset bundle folder_separately Add only folders as individual asset bundles folder_together Add only folders as one asset bundle regex_match Add assets matching regex to one asset bundle regex_match_delete Remove build info if filename matches regex regex_not_match_delete Remove build info if filename doesn't match regex same_name_together Add assets with same filename as one asset bundle You can also create custom strategies by extending TAssetBundleCompositionStrategy<Data>. AssetManager (Recommended) Pro edition only. AssetManager ships in the TAssetBundle.Extensions module, which is included with TAssetBundle Pro. The Lite (free) edition exposes the low-level TAssetBundles API directly — see the earlier sections of this manual. AssetManager (in TAssetBundle.Extensions) is the recommended way to load and manage assets. It provides automatic lifecycle management, usage tracking, and prefab pooling in one unified interface. Context-Based Loading The key feature of AssetManager is context-based loading. When you pass a GameObject as context, the asset is automatically linked to it. When the GameObject is destroyed, the asset reference is released — no manual cleanup needed. If the GameObject was never active (Unity does not call OnDestroy then), the reference is released by the next UnloadUnusedAssets(), UnloadUnusedAssetsAfterLastUse(), or GetUsingAssets() call. using UnityEngine; using UnityEngine.UI; using TAssetBundle.Extensions; public class ContextLoadingExample : MonoBehaviour { public string spritePath; void Start() { // Load and link to this GameObject // Asset is automatically released when this GameObject is destroyed AssetManager.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(gameObject, spritePath) .OnCompleted += asset => { GetComponent<Image>().sprite = asset.Get(); }; } // No OnDestroy cleanup needed! } You can also load with AssetRef for Inspector drag & drop: [AssetType(typeof(Sprite))] public AssetRef spriteRef; void Start() { AssetManager.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(gameObject, spriteRef) .OnCompleted += asset => { GetComponent<Image>().sprite = asset.Get(); }; } Manual Linking If you need to load without a context first, you can manually link the asset later: AssetManager.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(spritePath).OnCompleted += asset => { image.sprite = asset.Get(); image.LinkAsset(asset); // Manual link — auto-released when image is destroyed }; Prefab Pooling AssetManager integrates prefab loading from AssetBundles with automatic pooling: // Preload a prefab without instantiation await AssetManager.PreloadPrefabAsync("Assets/Prefabs/Bullet.prefab").ToTask(); // Load and instantiate from pool var bullet = await AssetManager.GetPrefabAsync("Assets/Prefabs/Bullet.prefab", parent).ToTask(); // Also works with AssetRef AssetManager.GetPrefabAsync(bulletAssetRef, transform).OnCompleted += go => { // use the instantiated prefab }; // Return to pool when done (not Destroy!) bullet.FreePrefab(); // Clear a specific prefab pool AssetManager.ClearPrefabPool("Assets/Prefabs/Bullet.prefab"); // Clear all prefab pools AssetManager.ClearPrefabPools(); Unloading Strategies AssetManager provides multiple unloading strategies: // Unload all loaded assets (also runs automatically on TAssetBundles.UnloadAll) AssetManager.UnloadAssetsAll(); // Unload only unused assets (reference count = 0) AssetManager.UnloadUnusedAssets(); // Unload assets unused for more than N seconds AssetManager.UnloadUnusedAssetsAfterLastUse(30f); // Unload a specific asset AssetManager.UnloadAsset("Assets/Sprites/icon.png"); AssetManager.UnloadAsset(myAssetRef); Usage Tracking Query loaded assets and their usage: // Iterate all assets currently in use foreach (var asset in AssetManager.GetUsingAssets()) { Debug.Log($"{asset.AssetPath} — UsageCount: {asset.UsageCount}"); } // Query a specific asset if (AssetManager.TryGetAssetInfo("Assets/Sprites/icon.png", out var info)) { Debug.Log($"Loaded: {info.IsLoaded}, Using: {info.IsUsing}"); } // Check if any assets are still loading bool loading = AssetManager.IsLoading(); // Protect an asset from auto-unloading info.SetDontDestroy(true); Use the Asset Usage Tracker editor window to visualize these relationships at runtime. Path Aliases Path Aliases let you refer to assets by a short, user-facing prefix instead of the full canonical catalog path. Assign a resolver to AssetManager.PathResolver once — every AssetManager API that takes a path string then translates aliases transparently before any catalog lookup or tracking occurs. Two ways to configure 1. Code — PrefixAliasResolver using TAssetBundle; using TAssetBundle.Extensions; var resolver = new PrefixAliasResolver { // Required only when any prefix has more than one folder. AssetExists = TAssetBundles.ExistAsset, }; // Single folder — the prefix is replaced by the folder. // A prefix ending with '/' keeps that '/' after the folder. resolver.Add("@char/", "Assets/Characters"); // Multiple folders — priority-ordered search path. // First folder that contains the asset wins (falls back to the first folder // when AssetExists is not set or no match is found). resolver.Add("@ui/", new[] { "Assets/DLC/UI", // checked first — DLC override "Assets/Shared/UI", // base fallback }); AssetManager.PathResolver = resolver; 2. Inspector — PathAliasTable ScriptableObject Right-click in the Project window and choose Create > TAssetBundle > Path Alias Table. Add entries in the Inspector: each entry has a prefix and one or more folders (drag folders directly from the Project window — FolderAssetRef uses GUID-based serialization). public PathAliasTable aliasTable; // assign in Inspector void Start() { // BuildResolver() wires AssetExists to TAssetBundles.ExistAsset automatically. AssetManager.PathResolver = aliasTable.BuildResolver(); } Loading with aliases // "@char/hero.prefab" resolves to "Assets/Characters/hero.prefab" AssetManager.GetPrefabAsync("@char/hero.prefab", parent); // Works with every AssetManager loading API AssetManager.LoadAssetAsync<Sprite>(gameObject, "@ui/icons/close.png"); AssetManager.PreloadPrefabAsync("@char/enemy.prefab"); Behavior notes Aliases are input-only. Return values, AssetInfo.AssetPath, event callbacks, and tracking keys all use canonical paths. This keeps logs, usage tracker, and manifest tooling consistent regardless of which alias was used to load the asset. Longer prefixes match first. @char/boss/ takes precedence over @char/ when both are registered — useful for nested namespaces. Joining. A prefix that ends with / keeps that / between the folder and the rest of the path, so "@char/" and "@char" both resolve "@char/hero.prefab" to "Assets/Characters/hero.prefab". Any other prefix is replaced by the folder as is. Caching. Single-folder results are cached. Multi-folder entries check the catalog on every call, so catalogs loaded later (including LoadCatalogInfoAsync) are used without a manual reset. Common use cases — DLC overrides (multi-folder priority search) and keeping call sites short when asset folder layouts are deep. See Sample03_PathAliasTable for a runnable example wiring a PathAliasTable to AssetManager.PathResolver. TAssetBundles (Low-Level API) For cases where you need direct control over asset handles, use the TAssetBundles API. You are responsible for manually unloading assets. Using Asset Path Load assets using their project path: using UnityEngine; using TAssetBundle; public class TestLoadAsset : MonoBehaviour { public string prefabPath; // Asset Path void Awake() { var loadAsset = TAssetBundles.LoadAssetAsync<GameObject>(prefabPath); loadAsset.OnComplete += (AssetHandle<GameObject> assetHandle) => { var asset = assetHandle.Get(); Instantiate(asset); }; } void OnDestroy() { TAssetBundles.UnloadAsset(prefabPath); } } Using Asset Reference Asset references allow drag-and-drop in the inspector and remain valid even if the asset is moved. using UnityEngine; using TAssetBundle; public class TestLoadAssetReference : MonoBehaviour { [AssetType(typeof(GameObject))] public AssetRef prefab; private AssetHandle prefabHandle; void Awake() { var loadAsset = TAssetBundles.LoadAssetAsync<GameObject>(prefab); loadAsset.OnComplete += (AssetHandle<GameObject> assetHandle) => { prefabHandle = assetHandle; var asset = assetHandle.Get(); Instantiate(asset); }; } void OnDestroy() { TAssetBundles.UnloadAsset(prefabHandle); } } Unloading Everything (UnloadAll) TAssetBundles.UnloadAll() unloads every loaded asset and AssetBundle at once (for example between game sessions, or right after UpdateCatalogAsync to apply new content immediately). Handles obtained before UnloadAll refer to unloaded assets. Releasing them with TAssetBundles.UnloadAsset(handle) is still safe and never affects anything loaded afterwards. Asset requests that have already started loading complete once as failures (AssetHandle.IsValid == false). Requests made afterwards start new loads; a new load of the same AssetBundle waits until the canceled one has ended. A scene request in progress completes once with an error logged and releases its scene bundle. If Unity was already loading the scene itself, Unity may still activate it — unload that scene yourself if it is not wanted. In the Editor Asset Mode nothing is destroyed, so requests in progress still succeed there; use the Asset Bundle Mode to test this behavior. TAssetBundles.OnUnloadedAll is raised afterwards. AssetManager subscribes to it automatically: all of its entries (including ones marked "Don't Destroy") and prefab pools are dropped, so the next AssetManager request loads again. Instances already taken out of a pool are not destroyed, but the assets they use are unloaded with their bundles, so spawn them again. // Drop your own caches of handles or loaded assets when everything is unloaded TAssetBundles.OnUnloadedAll += () => myIconCache.Clear(); // Apply a catalog update to content that is already loaded TAssetBundles.UpdateCatalogAsync().OnComplete += updated => { if (updated) { TAssetBundles.UnloadAll(); } }; Without UnloadAll, assets and AssetBundles that are already loaded keep being used after a catalog update until all their references are released. While such an AssetBundle is still loaded, an asset that the update added to it cannot be loaded (the request fails) until the AssetBundle is released. PrefabPoolManager Pro edition only. PrefabPoolManager ships in the TAssetBundle.Extensions module, which is included with TAssetBundle Pro. PrefabPoolManager provides standalone prefab pooling — independent of AssetBundles. Use this when you already have a prefab reference and want efficient reuse. using UnityEngine; using TAssetBundle.Extensions; public class PoolExample : MonoBehaviour { public GameObject bulletPrefab; void Start() { // Pre-allocate 20 instances PrefabPoolManager.Reserve(bulletPrefab, 20); } void Fire() { // Get from pool (creates new if pool is empty) var bullet = PrefabPoolManager.Get(bulletPrefab, transform); } void OnBulletHit(GameObject bullet) { // Return to pool instead of destroying bullet.FreePrefab(); } void OnDestroy() { // Clear the pool PrefabPoolManager.Clear(bulletPrefab); } } PrefabPoolManager also supports typed components: public Rigidbody projectilePrefab; void Fire() { var rb = PrefabPoolManager.Get(projectilePrefab, transform); rb.AddForce(transform.forward * 1000f); } Asynchronous Prefab Creation (Pro) PrefabPool.CreateAsync and PrefabPool.GetOrCreateAsync use Unity's asynchronous instantiation API and are available only when the Extensions assembly defines TASSETBUNDLE_INSTANTIATE_ASYNC: Unity [2022.3.20f1,2023.1) or 2023.3 and later (including Unity 6). They are not compiled for Unity 2021.3, 2023.1, or 2023.2. API reference snapshots generated against Unity 2021.3 therefore do not list these conditional methods. AssetManager.GetPrefabAsync remains available on older supported Unity versions for asynchronous prefab loading; its name does not mean that Unity's asynchronous instantiation APIs are available. The standalone PrefabPoolManager.Get and Reserve methods shown above instantiate synchronously. Remote Download Download AssetBundles from a remote server. Download Flow: Check for Catalog Update Update the Catalog Get the Download Size Download the Assets using UnityEngine; using UnityEngine.UI; using TAssetBundle; public class RemoteDownloadExample : MonoBehaviour { public string remoteDownloadUrl; public Text statusText; private void Awake() { // [BuildTarget] is replaced with actual platform TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl(remoteDownloadUrl); } private void OnGUI() { if (GUILayout.Button("Check Catalog Update")) { TAssetBundles.CheckCatalogUpdateAsync().OnComplete += result => { statusText.text = "Need update: " + result; }; } if (GUILayout.Button("Update Catalog")) { TAssetBundles.UpdateCatalogAsync().OnComplete += result => { statusText.text = "Update result: " + result; }; } if (GUILayout.Button("Get Download Size")) { TAssetBundles.GetDownloadSizeAsync().OnComplete += size => { statusText.text = "Size: " + FileSizeFormatter.FormatSize(size); }; } if (GUILayout.Button("Download All")) { var download = TAssetBundles.DownloadAsync(); download.OnProgress += info => { double percent = info.DownloadedSize / (double)info.TotalDownloadSize * 100; statusText.text = $"Downloading: {percent:0.0}%"; }; download.OnComplete += info => { statusText.text = info.IsDownloadComplete() ? "Complete!" : "Failed"; }; } } } When an update or a download fails: UpdateCatalogAsync returns false when there is nothing to update (the catalog is up to date, or the remote hash cannot be fetched), and when the catalog cannot be downloaded, cannot be read (corrupted, or built with other catalog settings) or cannot be saved. In these cases the catalog in use and the catalog saved on the device stay as they were, also after a restart, and OnCatalogLoaded is not raised. (This does not cover the app being killed or the device losing power while the catalog file is being replaced, or a failure of the operating system's file replace itself.) TAssetBundles.GetLastWebRequestError() holds the network or save error. Calling UpdateCatalogAsync again retries. On true the new catalog replaces the current one within the same frame, so requests made during the update are always served by one of the two catalogs. AssetBundles that are already loaded keep being used (see Unloading Everything). A download is complete only when every AssetBundle could be stored (IsDownloadComplete()). A failed AssetBundle has state == Failed and an Error; calling the download again fetches only what is still missing. With the separately managed cache (encrypted AssetBundles, WebGL, or Use Unity Remote AssetBundle Provider off) this includes a response that is not a valid AssetBundle or could not be written to the cache. A file enters this cache only once it is completely written, so a write interrupted by an error or by the app being closed is downloaded again (a power loss during the write is not covered). Starting without a remote URL: AssetBundles that are already cached load without a remote URL; the URL is needed only to fetch what is missing. An app can start from its saved catalog and cache before it knows the server address (for example when the address comes from your own backend), and set the URL only when something has to be downloaded. Without a remote URL, loading a remote AssetBundle uses only the cache and sends no remote HTTP request. An AssetBundle that is not cached fails at once, like any AssetBundle that cannot be loaded; loading never downloads for the separately managed cache, with or without a URL. This is not a guarantee of zero HTTP requests from the app. In WebGL, buildIncludeAssetBundle = All also makes the local provider check StreamingAssets/TA/<name>_<hash> on the page host, independently of the remote URL; a file that is not included can produce an HTTP 404. With the default BuiltinOnly, non-builtin AssetBundles do not cause these local-provider checks (included builtin AssetBundles still use the page host). The cache-only remote load does not contact the remote server; other providers and app code can still use the network. GetDownloadSize* counts only the AssetBundles that are not cached, with or without a URL. A download that has AssetBundles to fetch from the remote URL fails without sending a request: each of those AssetBundles is Failed with Error.errorType == EUnityWebRequestErrorResult.RemoteUrlNotSet, and IsDownloadComplete() is false (earlier versions returned an empty result with true). When nothing needs to be fetched the result is empty and complete, as before. GetLastWebRequestError() is not changed, since no request was made. The remote URL is saved on the device. A saved empty URL counts as not set, so the next start uses defaultRemoteUrl again: to start without a URL, call TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl("") before InitializeAsync on every start. AssetBundles handled by a plugin provider (such as Play Asset Delivery) are left out of the download result without a URL, as before: a pack that is not installed yet is fetched by that provider. This includes such AssetBundles whose hash changed in a catalog update, although those do need the remote URL — a load shows whether they are available. ExistAsset for every path plus a download size of 0 means the files are in the cache, not that they can be read: a damaged file, or one removed from the cache in the meantime, shows up only as a failed load. Treat a failed load as "needs the server": set the URL, download, and load again. On a first install the cache is empty, so the address for the first download has to come from outside the AssetBundles (defaultRemoteUrl or your own code). Play Asset Delivery packs are fetched by Google Play (on-demand packs use the network even without a remote URL). IEnumerator Boot(string[] startPaths) { TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl(""); // start from the cache only yield return TAssetBundles.InitializeAsync(); long size = -1; TAssetBundles.GetDownloadSizeByAssetsAsync(startPaths).OnComplete += s => size = s; yield return new WaitUntil(() => size >= 0); // A path missing from the catalog also has a download size of 0, so check it too. bool ready = size == 0 && startPaths.All(TAssetBundles.ExistAsset); if (!ready) { TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl(GetContentUrl()); // your code: default or from your backend AssetBundleDownloadInfo info = null; TAssetBundles.DownloadByAssetsAsync(startPaths).OnComplete += i => info = i; yield return new WaitUntil(() => info != null); if (!info.IsDownloadComplete()) { // info.downloads[i].state == Failed, info.downloads[i].Error: network, HTTP, cache write or RemoteUrlNotSet } } // Load; if a load still fails, set the URL, download and load again. } Updating content on the server: By default AssetBundle files are requested by name ({RemoteUrl}/{name}{extension}), without their hash, and the catalog decides which version is expected. If a new build overwrites the files of the previous one at the same URL, a device that still uses the previous catalog (its update failed, it is offline when checking, or the CDN still serves the old catalog) downloads new AssetBundle files under the previous version. They are cached as the previous version and can be combined with other previous-version AssetBundles already in the cache. The catalog cannot detect this: it records a hash for each AssetBundle but no checksum of the file content. There are two ways to avoid it: file names with the hash (below), or a separate folder per build. File names with the hash (Remote File Name With Hash): Turn on Remote File Name With Hash in the settings (off by default). Each build then also writes every AssetBundle as {name}_{hash}{extension} next to {name}{extension} in the output folder (same bytes), and the catalog it writes makes the runtime request {RemoteUrl}/{name}_{hash}{extension}. A device that still uses the previous catalog requests the previous hashed files, so it does not receive a newer file under an older version - as long as a published hashed file is never replaced. The runtime follows the catalog, not the settings of the app: each AssetBundle is requested the way its own catalog was built. A catalog built without the option, or by an earlier version (it has no such field), requests the plain names as before. With several catalogs, each follows its own. The cache is not affected: AssetBundles cached before the option was turned on (or with it off) stay cached and are not downloaded again. Turning the option on or off changes the catalog file once (devices download the catalog again, not the AssetBundles), and it does not invalidate the build cache (no rebuild). The first build after updating TAssetBundle changes the catalog file once in the same way, since the catalog now also stores the value (false when off). A hashed file that is not on the server fails the download (HTTP 404). The runtime never falls back to the plain name. A custom catalog serializer must write and read the remoteFileNameWithHash field of AssetCatalog. The build fails when the serializer loses it (the saved catalog is read back to check). A serializer in the app that drops the field makes that app request the plain names. The hash in the file name is not a content check: nothing verifies that the file under a hashed name holds that version. Never replace a published hashed file. Apps built with a version before this option, and devices that can still use a catalog built without it (a built-in catalog of an app that shipped without the option, or a catalog saved before the switch), request the plain names. As long as such apps or catalogs are in use, keep uploading the plain files with every build, as before. With Builtin AssetBundles Use Separate Folder, the plain files of built-in AssetBundles are in the separate …Builtin folder (their hashed files stay in the output folder); upload them to the same relative path on the server. Stopping the plain uploads, or removing them, is your decision once no such app or catalog is in use; leaving outdated plain files on the server while old apps read them is the worst case (they get mixed versions as described above). Publishing and keeping files (TAssetBundle does not upload or delete anything on your server): Upload the new *_{hash}{extension} files. Skip names that already exist on the server; never overwrite them. If apps or catalogs that use the plain names are still in use, upload the plain files (overwriting, as before). Upload the catalog ({catalogName}{catalogExtension}). Upload {catalogName}.hash last. This order keeps the update signal (.hash) from appearing before the files it points to. It is not atomic and not a guarantee: CDN propagation or caching can still show a device an older catalog or hash for a while (for example, the catalog is downloaded again later), and this option does not change that. The output folder holds only the current build; the server has to keep the hashed files of earlier builds. Do not mirror the output folder to the server with deletion (for example sync --delete): that removes the files earlier catalogs still request. Keep every hashed file referenced by any catalog a device may still use - remote catalogs published during your support period and the built-in catalogs of app versions you still support. Clean up only files outside that set. A separate folder per build (below) also works with this option: the hashed names do not replace the folder, and a catalog that can reach a folder needs its hashed files there. Validation scope of this option: Windows editor, Unity 2021.3.45f2 and 2022.3.62f2, StandaloneWindows64, both remote providers, a local HTTP test server. Also validated on one Samsung SM-G955N (Android 9, ARM64 IL2CPP, Unity 6000.3.18f1) using a device-local HTTP server with both remote providers. This does not cover PAD, real CDNs, or all Android devices; iOS and WebGL players remain unverified for this option. Other editor platforms and other Unity versions are not verified. A separate folder per build: Do not overwrite a published build: Upload every build to its own folder (for example https://cdn.example.com/builds/42/[BuildTarget]) and keep older folders while devices may still use them. Upload all files of a build before devices are pointed at it. Set defaultRemoteUrl of each app version to the folder of the build whose catalog ships in that app. To move devices to a newer build, call TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl(newFolder) and then UpdateCatalogAsync(). If it returns false, call SetRemoteUrl(previousFolder) again: the catalog in use is still the previous one, and its AssetBundles must come from its own folder. The remote URL is saved on the device (PlayerPrefs), so store the folder of the last successful update yourself and set it again at startup before loading remote content. void UpdateToBuild(string newFolder) { var previousFolder = PlayerPrefs.GetString("MyGame.ContentFolder", defaultFolder); TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl(newFolder); TAssetBundles.UpdateCatalogAsync().OnComplete += updated => { if (updated) { PlayerPrefs.SetString("MyGame.ContentFolder", newFolder); PlayerPrefs.Save(); } else { // Keep loading the content of the catalog that is still in use from its own folder. TAssetBundles.SetRemoteUrl(previousFolder); } }; } Download by Tags: // Get size for specific tags TAssetBundles.GetDownloadSizeByTagsAsync(new[] { "character", "level1" }); // Download specific tags TAssetBundles.DownloadByTagsAsync(new[] { "character" }); Download by Assets: // Download specific assets TAssetBundles.DownloadByAssetsAsync(new AssetRef[] { myAssetRef }); Download by Scenes: // Download scenes TAssetBundles.DownloadByScenesAsync(new[] { "MyScene" }); Device Cache Cleanup This is a Core feature shared by Lite and Pro. The methods return TAsyncOperation<CacheClearResult>: Method Selection ClearCacheByTagsAsync(string[]) Tags, using the current TagComparer ClearCacheByAssetsAsync(string[]) / ClearCacheByAssetsAsync(AssetRef[]) Asset paths / references ClearCacheByScenesAsync(string[]) / ClearCacheByScenesAsync(SceneAssetRef[]) Scene names or paths / references ClearUnusedCacheAsync() Old versions absent from current and temporary catalogs TAssetBundles.ClearCacheByAssetsAsync(new[] { "Assets/Levels/Level1.prefab" }).OnComplete += result => { Debug.Log($"Removed {result.DeletedCount}; managed-file bytes {result.DeletedFileBytes}"); foreach (var entry in result.Skipped) Debug.Log($"Kept {entry.AssetBundleName} ({entry.Hash}): {entry.Reason}"); }; Selected cleanup includes old hashes and unneeded dependencies; there is no dependency-inclusion option. It waits for Core downloads and performs deletion without yielding. Loaded/loading names are skipped (InUse). The exact dependency versions required by another cached, built-in, or conservatively retained provider bundle remain (RequiredByCachedAssetBundle); a deletion failure (DeleteFailed) also retains dependencies. Unity cache entries are cleared by exact cache name and hash, with same-name aliases handled together. Empty cache names are unsupported (UnsupportedCacheEntry). DeletedCount counts removed Unity versions and managed files. DeletedFileBytes counts managed files only, not Unity cache bytes. EditorAsset mode returns an empty result immediately. Only names in loaded current/temporary catalogs are inspected: unloaded catalogs and bundle names removed from all loaded catalogs are not reclaimed. Built-in files are not deleted. Existing disk-space automatic cleanup is unchanged; its in-use protection is outside this API's scope. TAssetBundle Settings Access via TAssetBundle > Settings menu. # Setting Description 1 Catalog Name Name of the catalog file 2 Output Folder AssetBundle build output folder; relative to the project, or a Windows drive-absolute path (see below) 3 Catalog Extension Catalog file extension 4 Bundle Extension AssetBundle file extension 5 Compress Catalog Enable catalog compression 6 Encrypt Catalog Enable catalog encryption 7 Encryption Key Key for encryption 8 Append Hash Add hash to asset bundle filename 9 Editor Play Mode Asset loading mode in editor 10 Force Remote Only Force remote AssetBundles in editor 11 Max Concurrent Requests Maximum concurrent web requests 12 Max Retry Count Maximum web request retries 13 Retry Wait Duration Wait time between retries 14 Use Build Cache Only build changed AssetBundles 15 Debug Log Enable debug logging 16 Include Catalog Include catalog in app 17 Embed Method How to embed AssetBundles 18 Recompress to LZ4 Recompress built-in bundles to LZ4 19 Use Unity Provider Use UnityRemoteAssetBundleProvider 20 Custom Catalog Serializer Custom catalog serializer 21 Custom Crypto Serializer Custom crypto serializer 22 Default Remote URL Default remote download URL, used at startup when no non-empty URL was saved with SetRemoteUrl — Explicit Asset Collection > Excluded Extensions (ExcludedExtensions) Case-insensitive explicit-root exclusions; defaults to .lighting. See Excluded Extensions. Remote File Name With Hash (below Builtin AssetBundles Use Separate Folder, off by default): the build also writes {name}_{hash}{extension} copies and the catalog makes the runtime request them. Build only - the runtime reads the value from the catalog. See Updating content on the server. Excluded Extensions Excluded from explicit collection; may still be included as a dependency. ExcludedExtensions affects direct registrations, folder leaves and composition-strategy candidates, not Unity's dependency closure. Extensions may include or omit the leading dot. Legacy settings receive .lighting once on first load; subsequent updates preserve customized and intentionally empty lists. Restore Default Exclusions (.lighting) restores the default. See Explicit Asset Collection for Ignore Assets and cache behavior. Building Asset Bundles Output folder and editor copies Relative output paths retain their existing layout: AssetBundle produces AssetBundle/<target> and the editor's local bundle copy remains in EditorRuntimeAssetBundle/<target>. Do not use relative paths containing parent-directory traversal (..): the existing relative-path contract can resolve the output and editor-copy directories to the same location, and the builder replaces the editor-copy target directory. This change does not alter that legacy behavior. On Windows, a drive-absolute output path such as D:\Builds\Out (or D:/Builds/Out, including a trailing separator) produces deployment files in D:/Builds/Out/<target>. The editor reads the catalog from that output, but keeps its local bundle copies inside the project, at EditorRuntime/Drive/D/Builds/Out/<target>. These copies are not added to the deployment output. Different drives are kept separate. With Remote File Name With Hash, the output folder has a {name}_{hash}{extension} copy of every AssetBundle of the catalog next to {name}{extension}, including built-in AssetBundles whose plain file moved to the separate …Builtin folder. The build cache keeps the plain names only, and the editor copies and the files added to the app keep their existing names; the hashed copies are made again by every build (also when all AssetBundles come from the build cache). Exclude the generated project EditorRuntime/ directory from version control, in addition to your existing editor-copy directories. Each build replaces only the selected output's editor-copy target directory. Changing Output Folder does not remove copies left by previous settings; clearing the build cache does not remove these copies either. Do not place unrelated files in generated output or editor-copy target directories, or nest one output inside another output's target directory. Validation scope: Windows editor, Unity 2021.3.45f2 and 2022.3.62f2, StandaloneWindows64, relative and Windows drive-absolute outputs. UNC inputs map separately to EditorRuntime/UNC/<server>/<share>/.../<target>, but actual network-share I/O is unverified. macOS/Linux execution, paths over 260 characters, other build targets (including Android), and drive-root output are not verified by this change. Windows root-relative (\Out), drive-relative (D:Out), and extended/device (\\?\...) paths are outside this supported path contract. Build command After configuring your manifests, build AssetBundles via TAssetBundle > Build Asset Bundle menu. Build Features: Incremental Build: Only changed bundles are rebuilt (when Build Cache is enabled). The cache tracks file hashes (MD5) and propagates changes through the full dependency graph — both forward and reverse. Automatic Dependency Management: Dependencies between bundles are handled automatically Cross-Platform: Build for any supported platform Plugin System TAssetBundle supports a plugin architecture for extending its functionality. Plugins can hook into: Build Pipeline — Add custom build steps (e.g., copying bundles to asset packs) Runtime Loading — Provide custom asset bundle loading providers Inspector UI — Add per-manifest configuration UI Plugins are implemented as ScriptableObject assets (PluginBase) with associated plugin modules (PluginModuleBase<T>) discovered via the [PluginModule] attribute. 👉 Plugin Development Guide — step-by-step guide to building your own plugin, with module interfaces, per-manifest data, and execution order. Included Plugin: Play Asset Delivery The Play Asset Delivery plugin demonstrates the plugin system. It integrates Google Play's asset pack system for Android AAB builds, allowing bundles to be delivered via install-time, fast-follow, or on-demand delivery. See the TAssetBundlePlugins/PlayAssetDelivery/ folder for details. Editor Tools TAssetBundle Browser A unified view of all manifests and bundles. Access via TAssetBundle > TAssetBundle Browser. Features: Search: Filter manifests by name, or search assets across all manifests Sort: Sort by Name, Bundle Count, or Asset Count Show Options: Toggle included, not included, or ignored assets Toolbar Actions: Button Description Clear All Asset Bundle Build Infos Remove all bundle configurations Run All Composition Strategy Execute strategies on all manifests Build Asset Bundle Build all configured bundles Check Dependencies Analyze bundle dependencies TAssetBundle Menu # Menu Item Description 1 Settings Open TAssetBundle Settings 2 Clear Build Cache Remove build cache for current platform 3 Build Asset Bundle Build AssetBundles 4 Run All Composition Strategy Run strategies on all manifests 5 Clear All Composition Strategy Clear all manifest build info 6 Open Build Folder Open build output folder 7 Open Cache Folder Open downloaded assets cache folder 8 Clear Cached Assets Remove downloaded asset cache 9 TAssetBundle Browser Open browser window 10 Tag Editor Open tag editor 11 Web Server Test Open web server test window 12 Catalog Diff Compare two catalogs and list changed bundles 13 Dependency Checker Check AssetBundle dependencies 14 Asset Reference Tracker Track active assets at runtime Catalog Diff Compare two asset catalogs and see exactly which bundles changed between them. Useful before shipping a content update — you can confirm that only the bundles you expected were rebuilt, and check how much the download size moved. Access via TAssetBundle > Catalog Diff. Usage: Catalog A (current) is prefilled with the catalog of the active build target, if it exists. Catalog B (comparison target) is remembered from your last comparison; use Browse to pick either one. Press Compare. The diff is reported in the B → A direction, so B is treated as the older catalog and A as the newer one. What it shows: Catalog Info — a B → A comparison of the catalog header (TAssetBundle version, catalog version, build number, bundle version, MD5 hash, file size). Values that differ are shown in bold. Added / Removed / Modified / Unchanged sections — each bundle is grouped by its diff state, with a count per section. Toggle sections with the filter checkboxes and narrow the list with the search field. Per-bundle detail — expand a bundle row to see its hash transition (Modified) and the individual asset paths that were added or removed. Each asset and the manifest that owns the bundle are shown as ObjectFields, so you can click through to them in the Project window. Size summary — per-bundle size delta for Modified bundles, total size for Added/Removed bundles. Warnings: The window warns you when a comparison is likely to be misleading: The two catalogs report different catalogVersion values (schema mismatch). The two catalog paths appear to belong to different build targets (for example, comparing an Android catalog against a StandaloneWindows64 one). Asset Usage Tracker Pro edition only. This editor window depends on AssetManager bookkeeping and ships with the TAssetBundle.Extensions module. The Lite edition includes the runtime Asset Reference Tracker (under TAssetBundle > Asset Reference Tracker) which shows currently loaded assets; Usage Tracker adds GameObject-level visibility on top. Track which GameObjects are using which assets during play mode. This works with AssetManager's context-based loading and LinkAsset. Access via TAssetBundle > Extensions > Asset Usage Tracker. Features: View assets in use, with the number of linked GameObjects and how long each asset has been loaded View the GameObjects linked to each asset, and how long each link has been held Show Active / Show Inactive filters, sort by name, path, or load time, and regex search Find GameObjects that still hold assets you expected to be released Editor Play Modes TAssetBundle supports two play modes in the editor: Editor Asset Mode (Development) Load assets directly without building AssetBundles. Fast iteration during development. Go to TAssetBundle > Settings Set Editor Play Mode to Editor Asset Asset Bundle Mode (Testing) Load assets from built AssetBundles. Test production behavior. Build your AssetBundles first Go to TAssetBundle > Settings Set Editor Play Mode to Asset Bundle Sample Materials on URP The bundled samples include materials that use Built-in render pipeline shaders. New Unity 6 projects default to URP, where those shaders are not compatible — sample meshes render as pink. This is a one-time project-wide fix: Open Window > Rendering > Render Pipeline Converter. Select Built-in to URP (or Built-in to HDRP for HDRP projects) in the dropdown. Check Material Shader Converter. Click Initialize Converters to scan, then Convert Assets to apply. The converter rewrites the materials in place; the samples then render correctly under your project's render pipeline.
